stories.title: Russia conducting 'surgical operation' in Ukraine to avoid harming civilians — TASS chief
stories.summary: Andrey Kondrashov presented the Airport documentary film, which he directed
article_sentences: SYKTYVKAR, August 21.

Russia is conducting a "surgical operation" as part of its special military operation to avoid harming civilians and civilian infrastructure, TASS Director General Andrey Kondrashov told reporters in Syktyvkar during the CIS International Film Festival currently taking place in the Russian northeastern Komi Region.
We are afraid of damaging infrastructure used exclusively by civilians, not the military, and we are also afraid - God forbid - of causing completely unjustified civilian casualties.
We will continue to act this way up to a certain limit.
For those who are currently preparing to fight us, however, the conversation will be entirely different," Kondrashov noted.
He presented the Airport documentary film, which he directed, at the CIS International Film Festival in Syktyvkar.
The film provides a detailed account of the first battle for the survival of the Donbass, drawing on archival footage and eyewitness accounts of the events.

In particular, it features Donetsk Airport press secretary Dmitry Kosinov, Donetsk physician Andrey Boryak, DPR Hero and Russian presidential envoy in the Ural Federal District Artyom Zhoga, as well as residents of Donetsk.
In 2014, the Prokofiev Donetsk Airport became one of the hotbeds in the conflict between Ukrainian forces and Donbass militias.
On May 26, 2014, the last flight departed from the airport, bound for Kiev.
Fighting then broke out on the airport grounds and continued until mid-January 2015.
The film is available to watch for free on the Russian Smotrim media platform.

stories.title: Iran’s Navy to continue defending country's interests in Strait of Hormuz — commander
stories.summary: Rear Admiral Shahram Irani said the Navy has a strong presence in the straits
article_sentences: RABAT, August 21.
Iran’s Navy is present in the Strait of Hormuz and other Gulf straits and will defend them against any enemy attacks, Iranian Navy commander Rear Admiral Shahram Irani said.
"The Navy has a strong presence in the straits and strategically important waterways in the Gulf," he said, as cited by the Al Mayadeen television channel.

The Iranian Navy "continues to defend Iran’s national interests and security in the Gulf," he stressed, adding that the Navy "is fighting the enemies with all its might and will not let them get close."

stories.title: Russian authorities optimizing refineries’ maintenance schedules to stabilize fuel market
stories.summary: The cabinet of ministers discussed the implementation of measures aimed at ensuring sufficient fuel supplies for the domestic market
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 21.

Russian authorities have set a goal to optimize maintenance schedules of oil refineries to minimize the risk of supply shortages in the fuel market, the cabinet reported following a meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak.
"The need for an even distribution of available fuel supplies among and within the regions was emphasized.
A task was set to optimize planned refinery maintenance schedules to minimize the risk of supply shortages in the market," the report said.

Participants of the meeting discussed the implementation of measures aimed at ensuring sufficient fuel supplies for the domestic market, maintaining fair prices, and increasing transparency in fuel sales across both wholesale and retail segments.
"Emphasis was placed on the need for an equitable distribution of available fuel supplies among regions and within them," according to the report.
On July 30, the Russian government imposed a new temporary ban on the export of gasoline, diesel, and other types of fuel, effective until January 31, 2027.
The decision was made to maintain stability in the domestic fuel market.
The cabinet also suspended the special rules for determining prices in state procurement of motor fuel until the end of 2026.
Moreover, the government adopted a resolution aimed at ensuring agricultural producers are supplied with the necessary volumes of motor fuel.

Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told TASS earlier that Russia had secured sufficient fuel supplies to meet domestic market needs, but a surge in panic buying had driven up demand by around 20-30%, adding that government measures to stabilize the fuel market were yielding results as limits were already being lifted in several regions, with the number of operational filling stations increasing, and queues shortening.
